newsitem.title: UK: Amersham deal sparks mixed share reviews. [CORRECTED 11:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Amersham deal sparks mixed share reviews. [CORRECTED 11:15 GMT]

text.p: Amersham International Plc shares got a mixed review a day after the British health and technology group said it would merge with Norwegian group Nycomed ASA.
Shares jumped 117-1/2p to 18 sterling before easing back by 1026 GMT to 17.80 sterling, up 97-1/2p.
The stock catapulted 16 percent on Tuesday to a record high of 18.50 sterling before closing at 16.82-1/2 sterling. It has rallied by more than two-thirds since the start of the year.
BZW cut its rating on the stock to "hold" and NatWest downgraded from "add" to "hold", market sources said. Analysts were not available for comment.
Yet other analysts remained positive on the stock.

Kleinwort Benson reiterated its "buy" rating and raised its price forecast to 19.00 stg from 17.00 sterling, said analyst Steve Putnam. He said he raised 1998 and 1999 earnings by 20 percent to 98 pence and 118 pence per share, respectively.
"(The deal) was very positive," he said.
Pharmaceutical analyst James Culverwell at Merrill Lynch said he maintained his "buy" rating (corrects from reiterated his "accumulate" rating) with a target of 21.00 stg.
"We have been buyers and are still buyers," he said.
He raised his 1998 earnings forecast by 20 percent to 105 pence per share.
Amersham said it would merge with Nycomed to form a world leader in the fast-growing field of diagnostic technology, including traditional X-rays and a revolution in use of ultrasound.
The agreement follows the June 10 announced that Amersham was to combine its drug test equipment arm with Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc's to carve out another world-leading position.
